uncited: This family encompasses methods for evaluating continuous fields along rays (via polynomial composition) and resampling discrete volume data (via spatial convolution) to support direct volume ray casting.

It is distinguished from sibling methods like [Pre-Integration Lookup](2854-pre-integration-lookup.md) by focusing on the algebraic or spatial mechanics of data evaluation rather than lookup-table optimization or surface-based compositing.

The methods in this family share the goal of mapping 3D data to 1D ray values or resampling grids, but they differ fundamentally in domain and mechanism. [Composition via Convolution (Power Form)](1591-composition-via-convolution-power-form.md) operates in the algebraic domain, composing trivariate polynomials with linear ray parameterizations to produce univariate polynomials. [Feed-Backward Reconstruction](2433-feed-backward-reconstruction.md) operates in the spatial domain, using convolution kernels to resample discrete signals.
No single mathematical formulation or data structure is shared across both; they are grouped here by their role in the reconstruction/compositing pipeline of volume rendering.
These techniques are used in direct volume visualization pipelines where accurate field evaluation or resampling is critical for image quality.
